properties.displayName: LLMD-001 Direct prompt injection phrasing in user prompt
properties.description:
A user prompt contains well-known instruction-override phrasing ("ignore all previous
instructions", "you are now unrestricted", Hungarian "felejtsd el a korábbi utasításokat").
Keyword matching only catches unsophisticated attempts; pair it with LLMD-003 (canary)
to learn whether an attempt actually succeeded.
properties.query:
let injection = @"(?i)\b(ignore|disregard|forget|override)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(previous|prior|above|earlier|preceding|system)\b[^.\n]{0,20}\b(instructions?|prompts?|rules|directions|guidelines)\b|\bnew instructions?\s*:|\byou are now\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(unrestricted|unfiltered|uncensored)\b|(felejtsd el|hagyd figyelmen k[ií]v[üu]l|ne vedd figyelembe)[^.\n]{0,30}(kor[áa]bbi|el[őo]z[őo]|fenti|eddigi)[^.\n]{0,15}utas[íi]t[áa]s";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
| where prompt matches regex injection
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, app_name, model,
          MatchedPhrase = extract(injection, 0, prompt), prompt

properties.displayName: LLMD-002 Instructions aimed at the model inside retrieved content
properties.description:
A chunk returned by the retriever contains text addressed to the AI (instruction-override
phrasing, "note to the AI assistant", templated image URLs). This means a poisoned document
is in the index and is being served into model context. It fires whether or not the model
obeyed; LLMD-007 tells you if it did. Triage starts with doc_id and doc_source: who uploaded it.
properties.query:
let injection = @"(?i)\b(ignore|disregard|forget|override)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(previous|prior|above|earlier|preceding|system)\b[^.\n]{0,20}\b(instructions?|prompts?|rules|directions|guidelines)\b|\bnew instructions?\s*:|\byou are now\b[^.\n]{0,30}\b(unrestricted|unfiltered|uncensored)\b|(felejtsd el|hagyd figyelmen k[ií]v[üu]l|ne vedd figyelembe)[^.\n]{0,30}(kor[áa]bbi|el[őo]z[őo]|fenti|eddigi)[^.\n]{0,15}utas[íi]t[áa]s";
let addressed_to_model = @"(?i)\b(note|message|instructions?) (to|for) the (ai|assistant|ai assistant|llm|model)\b|\bassistant instructions\s*:|\b(ai|llm) (assistant|agent)\s*:|!\[[^\]]*\]\(https?://[^)\s]*\{[^}]*\}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "retrieval"
| where chunk_text matches regex injection or chunk_text matches regex addressed_to_model
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Retrievals = count(), Prompts = make_set(request_id, 10)
    by session_id, user_id, src_ip, doc_id, doc_source, doc_title
| extend TimeGenerated = FirstSeen

properties.displayName: LLMD-003 System prompt canary token in model output
properties.description:
The application plants a unique canary string in its system prompt (here: sp-canary-<16 hex>).
The string has no business reason to appear in any output, so a hit is a confirmed system
prompt leak regardless of how the attacker phrased the request. This is the highest-precision
rule in the pack. Rotate the canary per deployment and keep the pattern in sync.
properties.query:
let canary = @"sp-canary-[0-9a-f]{16}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type in ("completion", "tool_call")
| extend Output = iff(event_type == "completion", completion, tool_args)
| where Output matches regex canary
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, event_type, tool_name,
          Canary = extract(canary, 0, Output), Output

properties.displayName: LLMD-004 Credentials or financial identifiers in model output or tool arguments
properties.description:
A completion, or the arguments of a tool call, contains a secret or financial identifier:
AWS access keys, a secret next to a 40 character key, PEM private keys, GitHub and Slack
tokens, Hungarian IBANs. Checking tool arguments matters: in agentic exfiltration the secret
leaves through send_email or http_get and never shows up in the chat answer.
Pattern matching is defeated by reformatting (see docs/coverage.md, evade-spaced-secret).

properties.displayName: LLMD-005 Auto-loading image with query string to external host in model output
properties.description:
The model emitted a markdown image or HTML img tag that points to a non-corporate host and
carries a query string. Chat clients that render markdown fetch the image without a click, so
whatever is in the query string (often conversation content) reaches the attacker's server.
Reference-style images ("![x][r]" with a separate "[r]: URL" line) are included: that variant
bypassed link redaction in EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711, Microsoft 365 Copilot). Clickable links are
deliberately out of scope because they are too common in normal answers; see docs/coverage.md.
properties.query:
let corporate_domain = "acme-freight.hu";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "completion"
| where completion contains "](http" or completion contains "<img" or completion contains "]: http"
| extend InlineUrls = extract_all(@"(?:!\[[^\]]*\]\(|<img[^>]+src=[""']?)(https?://[^)\s""'>]+)", completion)
// Reference-style images (![alt][ref] + a "[ref]: URL" line) slipped past link redaction in EchoLeak
| extend RefImage = completion matches regex @"!\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]+\]"
| extend RefUrls = iff(RefImage, extract_all(@"(?m)^\s*\[[^\]]+\]:\s*(https?://\S+)", completion), dynamic([]))
| extend ImageUrls = array_concat(InlineUrls, RefUrls)
| mv-expand ImageUrl = ImageUrls to typeof(string)
| extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(ImageUrl).Host)), Query = tostring(parse_url(ImageUrl)["Query Parameters"])
| where ImageUrl contains "?"
// Exact match or a true subdomain; "has" or "contains" would accept acme-freight.hu.evil.com
| where not(Host == corporate_domain or Host endswith strcat(".", corporate_domain))
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, Host, ImageUrl, Query, completion

properties.displayName: LLMD-006 Side-effecting agent tool aimed at an external destination
properties.description:
The assistant called a tool that moves data out (send_email, http_get) with a target outside
the corporate domain and the HTTP allowlist. An agent that can email arbitrary recipients is
an exfiltration channel the moment it reads attacker-controlled text. Tune the two lists to
your environment; anything allowlisted is a blind spot (see evade-allowlisted-exfil).
properties.query:
let corporate_domain = "acme-freight.hu";
let http_allowlist = dynamic(["learn.microsoft.com", "github.com"]);
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_name in ("send_email", "http_get")
| extend Target = tolower(tool_target)
| where not(Target == corporate_domain or Target endswith strcat(".", corporate_domain))
| where not(tool_name == "http_get" and Target in (http_allowlist))
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, tool_name, Target, tool_status, tool_args

properties.displayName: LLMD-007 Egress tool call shortly after externally sourced content entered context
properties.description:
Correlation of LLMD-006 with retrieval: in the same session, a document that did not come from
the internal wiki was pulled into context, and within 10 minutes the agent sent data to an
external destination. This is the shape of a successful indirect prompt injection: the user
asked an ordinary question and the agent acted on instructions from the document.

properties.displayName: LLMD-008 Burst of agent tool calls in one session
properties.description:
Ten or more tool calls in a single session within five minutes. Normal assistant turns use zero
to two tools; an agent looping over the document store, probing paths or retrying denied calls
looks different. Denied calls are surfaced separately because path traversal attempts show up
as denials.

properties.displayName: LLMD-009 Token consumption spike per identity
properties.description:
One identity consumed more than 50 000 tokens within a one hour activity window. Typical
cause: a leaked API key or service credential used to run unrelated workloads on your bill
(cost harvesting), or a scripted denial-of-wallet. The fixed threshold is a starting point;
in production replace it with a per-user baseline (for example series_decompose_anomalies over
14 days). Abuse spread thinly under the threshold is not caught (evade-slow-consumption).
properties.query:
let threshold = 50000;
let trigger_window = 1h;  // see LLMD-008: dedupe across overlapping runs
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "completion"
| sort by user_id asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend Window = row_window_session(TimeGenerated, 1h, 30m, user_id != prev(user_id))
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), LastRequest = max(TimeGenerated), Tokens = sum(input_tokens + output_tokens), Requests = count(),
            Sessions = make_set(session_id, 20), SourceIps = make_set(src_ip, 10)
    by user_id, Window
| where Tokens > threshold and LastRequest > ago(trigger_window)
| project-away Window

properties.displayName: LLMD-010 Repeated guardrail blocks from one identity
properties.description:
Three or more prompts from the same user blocked by the input guardrail within ten minutes.
A single block is noise (curiosity, a copy-pasted meme); a series is someone iterating on a
jailbreak. Works with any guardrail that logs its decisions, for example Azure AI Content
Safety Prompt Shields or Llama Prompt Guard, as long as the block becomes a guardrail event.
properties.query:
let threshold = 3;
let trigger_window = 10m;  // see LLMD-008: dedupe across overlapping runs
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "guardrail" and guardrail_action == "block"
| sort by user_id asc, TimeGenerated asc
| extend Window = row_window_session(TimeGenerated, 10m, 10m, user_id != prev(user_id))
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), LastBlock = max(TimeGenerated), Blocks = count(),
            Rules = make_set(guardrail_rule), SamplePrompts = make_list(prompt, 5),
            Sessions = make_set(session_id), SourceIps = make_set(src_ip)
    by user_id, Window
| where Blocks >= threshold and LastBlock > ago(trigger_window)
| extend src_ip = tostring(SourceIps[0])
| project-away Window

properties.displayName: LLMD-011 Obfuscated content in user prompt (base64, Unicode tags, zero-width)
properties.description:
The prompt carries content a human reviewer would not read directly: a long base64 blob,
invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000 to U+E007F, used for "ASCII smuggling"), or runs of
zero-width characters. The query decodes the payload so the analyst sees what was hidden.
properties.query:
let b64 = @"[A-Za-z0-9+/]{60,}={0,2}";
let unicode_tags = @"[\x{E0000}-\x{E007F}]";
let zero_width = @"[\x{200B}-\x{200D}\x{2060}\x{FEFF}]{3,}";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
// Real base64 of text mixes upper and lower case; hex digests (SHA-256, commit IDs) do not.
| extend B64Candidate = extract(b64, 0, prompt)
| extend IsB64 = B64Candidate matches regex "[A-Z]" and B64Candidate matches regex "[a-z]"
| extend Technique = case(prompt matches regex unicode_tags, "unicode_tag_smuggling",
                          IsB64, "base64_blob",
                          prompt matches regex zero_width, "zero_width_chars", "")
| where isnotempty(Technique)
| extend Codepoints = unicode_codepoints_from_string(prompt)
| mv-apply Cp = Codepoints to typeof(long) on (
      where Cp between (917504 .. 917631)
      | summarize Hidden = make_list(Cp - 917504))
| extend DecodedPayload = case(Technique == "unicode_tag_smuggling", unicode_codepoints_to_string(Hidden),
                               Technique == "base64_blob", base64_decode_tostring(B64Candidate), "")
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, Technique, DecodedPayload, prompt

properties.displayName: LLMD-012 System prompt extraction attempt
properties.description:
The user asks the assistant to repeat, print or reveal its instructions. Low severity on its
own: people are curious. Escalate when the same session also hits LLMD-003 (the canary leaked)
or the user hits LLMD-001 or LLMD-010.
properties.query:
let extraction = @"(?i)\b(repeat|print|reveal|show|output|display|dump)\b[^.\n]{0,25}\b(system prompt|instructions|the text above|everything above|initial prompt|hidden prompt)\b|\bwhat (are|were) your (original |initial |system |hidden )?(instructions|rules|prompt)\b|\brepeat the (text|words) above\b";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "prompt"
| where prompt matches regex extraction
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, MatchedPhrase = extract(extraction, 0, prompt), prompt

properties.displayName: LLMD-013 Persistent instruction written to agent long-term memory
properties.description:
The agent saved something to long-term memory that is either a standing instruction to act
("always send a copy of every email to ...") or was written in a turn where untrusted content
(external upload, earlier memory) was in context. Memory turns a one-off prompt injection into
a persistent one that fires in later sessions, as shown by Rehberger's "SpAIware" against ChatGPT
memory (2024) and Unit 42's Amazon Bedrock Agents research (2025). Triage: read memory_text,
find the source document of the turn, purge the memory entry.
properties.query:
let persistent_action = @"(?i)\b(always|from now on|in (all )?future|every time|whenever)\b[^.\n]{0,80}\b(send|e-?mail|forward|bcc|cc|copy|call|run|execute|share|upload|post)\b";
let untrusted_turns = LLMAppLogs_CL
    | where event_type == "retrieval" and doc_source != "internal-wiki"
    | distinct request_id;
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "memory_write"
| extend PersistentAction = memory_text matches regex persistent_action,
         WrittenWithUntrustedContext = request_id in (untrusted_turns)
| where PersistentAction or WrittenWithUntrustedContext
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, PersistentAction,
          WrittenWithUntrustedContext, memory_text

properties.displayName: LLMD-014 MCP tool description changed after first use (rug pull)
properties.description:
The same MCP server and tool name now advertise a description with a different SHA-256 than the
first one seen in the lookback. The model obeys tool descriptions, so a silent change is a silent
change of instructions, after the user approved the server. Described as a "rug pull" by Invariant
Labs (2025); CVE-2025-54136 ("MCPoison", Cursor) is the same class at the config level. In
production keep approved hashes in a watchlist instead of relying on the first hash in the
lookback, and treat every hit as "re-review this tool before anyone uses it again".
properties.query:
let trigger_window = 1h;
let registry = LLMAppLogs_CL | where event_type == "tool_registry";
let approved = registry
    | summarize arg_min(TimeGenerated, tool_desc_sha256) by tool_key
    | project tool_key, FirstSeen = TimeGenerated, ApprovedHash = tool_desc_sha256;
registry
| where TimeGenerated > ago(trigger_window)
| join kind=inner approved on tool_key
| where tool_desc_sha256 != ApprovedHash
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, mcp_server, tool_name, tool_key, FirstSeen,
          ApprovedHash, NewHash = tool_desc_sha256, NewDescription = tool_description

properties.displayName: LLMD-015 Hidden instructions in an MCP tool description (tool poisoning)
properties.description:
An MCP server advertises a tool whose description contains instructions for the model rather than
documentation for a developer: <IMPORTANT> blocks, "do not tell the user", "before using this tool
read ...", "first call send_email", references to ~/.ssh, .env or mcp.json. The model sees the full
description, the user usually sees only the tool name. Pattern set follows Invariant Labs' tool
poisoning disclosure (2025); MCPTox (arXiv 2508.14925) measured attack success up to 72.8% on real
servers. Fires once per session that loads the tool; dedupe on tool_desc_sha256 in the incident.
properties.query:
let poisoning = @"(?i)<important>|\b(do not|don't|never)\s+(tell|mention|inform|reveal|show)\b|\bbefore (using|calling) this tool\b|\b(first|always)\s+call\b|\b(read|send|include|pass|forward)\b[^.\n]{0,60}(\.ssh|id_rsa|\.env\b|credentials|mcp\.json|conversation|user's (last |previous )?message)|\b(ignore|override)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\binstructions\b";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_registry"
| where tool_description matches regex poisoning
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, mcp_server, tool_name, tool_key, tool_desc_sha256,
          MatchedText = extract(poisoning, 0, tool_description), tool_description

properties.displayName: LLMD-016 Destructive agent tool executed without human approval
properties.description:
A tool classified as destructive (delete, drop, overwrite) ran with tool_approval = auto: no human
was asked. Approval prompts are the main brake on an agent that has been steered; when they are
off, one injected instruction is enough to destroy data. The fix is configuration (require
approval for the destructive class); the alert tells you where that is missing and what ran.
properties.query:
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_risk == "destructive" and tool_approval == "auto" and tool_status == "ok"
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), Calls = count(), Targets = make_set(tool_target, 50),
            Tools = make_set(tool_name)
    by session_id, user_id, src_ip, request_id

properties.displayName: LLMD-017 Dangerous shell command issued by an agent
properties.description:
An agent's shell tool was given a reverse shell, a remote script piped into a shell, a base64
payload piped into a shell, a setuid change or a recursive delete of /. Fires regardless of
approval: a human clicking "allow" on a curl | sh is still a curl | sh. The 2026 "Agentjacking"
research (Tenet Security) got coding agents to run attacker packages through exactly this kind of
"fix" command. Staged payloads (the command only runs a file dropped earlier) are not caught.
properties.query:
let dangerous = @"/dev/(tcp|udp)/|\bbash\s+-i\b|\bnc(at)?\b[^|;]{0,40}\s-(e|c)\b|\bmkfifo\b|\bsocat\b|\b(curl|wget)\b[^|;]{0,200}\|\s*(sudo\s+)?(ba|z|da)?sh\b|base64\s+(-d|--decode)[^|;]{0,80}\|\s*(ba)?sh\b|\bchmod\s+[ugo]*\+s\b|\brm\s+-[a-zA-Z]*r[a-zA-Z]*\s+/(\s|$|\*)|\bpython[0-9.]*\s+-c\s+[^|]{0,80}socket";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_risk == "exec"
| where tool_args matches regex dangerous
| project TimeGenerated, user_id, src_ip, session_id, request_id, tool_name, tool_approval,
          MatchedText = extract(dangerous, 0, tool_args), tool_args

properties.displayName: LLMD-018 Credential material targeted through agent tools
properties.description:
An agent tool was pointed at files that hold credentials: cloud CLI credentials, SSH keys, .env
files, .git-credentials, kube and docker configs, and MCP client configuration (mcp.json holds the
tokens for every connected server). Counts denied attempts too: a denied read of ~/.aws/credentials
is still someone trying. CVE-2026-75130 (Context7 MCP) used poisoned instructions to make agents
exfiltrate .env files.
properties.query:
let cred_paths = @"(?i)(\.aws/(credentials|config)|\.ssh/|\bid_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)\b|(^|[/\s""])\.env\b|\.git-credentials|\.netrc|\.kube/config|\.docker/config\.json|mcp\.json|/etc/shadow|\.azure/|gcloud/credentials)";
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_name in ("read_file", "run_shell", "write_file", "http_get")
| where tool_target matches regex cred_paths or tool_args matches regex cred_paths
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(TimeGenerated), Attempts = count(), Denied = countif(tool_status == "denied"),
            Targets = make_set(tool_args, 20)
    by session_id, user_id, src_ip

properties.displayName: LLMD-019 Private data read and sent out in the same turn (lethal trifecta)
properties.description:
Within one user turn the agent read a private file and then sent data to an external party: an
email or HTTP request outside the corporate domain and allowlist, or a call to a third-party MCP
server. Simon Willison's "lethal trifecta" (2025) names the three ingredients of agent data theft:
private data, untrusted content, external communication. This rule fires on the last two in
sequence; the untrusted leg is covered by LLMD-002, -007, -015 and -021. The GitHub MCP exploit
(Invariant Labs, 2025) and the Supabase MCP leak (General Analysis, 2025) both have this shape.
properties.query:
let corporate_domain = "acme-freight.hu";
let http_allowlist = dynamic(["learn.microsoft.com", "github.com"]);
let private_reads = LLMAppLogs_CL
    | where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_name == "read_file" and tool_status == "ok"
    | project ReadAt = TimeGenerated, request_id, ReadTarget = tool_target;
LLMAppLogs_CL
| where event_type == "tool_call" and tool_status == "ok"
| extend Target = tolower(tool_target)
| where tool_risk == "external"
    or (tool_name in ("send_email", "http_get")
        and not(Target == corporate_domain or Target endswith strcat(".", corporate_domain))
        and not(tool_name == "http_get" and Target in (http_allowlist)))
| project SentAt = TimeGenerated, request_id, session_id, user_id, src_ip, tool_name, Target
| join kind=inner private_reads on request_id
| where SentAt >= ReadAt
| summarize TimeGenerated = min(SentAt), PrivateReads = make_set(ReadTarget), Sinks = make_set(Target),
            SinkTools = make_set(tool_name)
    by session_id, user_id, src_ip, request_id

properties.displayName: LLMD-020 Agent modifies its own or another agent's configuration
properties.description:
An agent wrote to AI-agent configuration: editor agent settings (.vscode/settings.json, .cursor/),
Claude Code settings, MCP client configs (mcp.json), or instruction files that agents auto-load
(AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, copilot-instructions.md). This is how an injection becomes privilege
escalation: CVE-2025-53773 (GitHub Copilot) had the agent set chat.tools.autoApprove ("YOLO mode")
and then run commands; CVE-2025-54135 (Cursor) had it write a new .cursor/mcp.json. DisablesApproval
marks writes that switch approval prompts off.

properties.displayName: LLMD-021 Instructions aimed at the agent inside a tool result
properties.description:
A tool returned text addressed to the AI rather than data: instruction-override phrasing, "AI
agent: ...", "no need to ask the user", or a "to fix this error run `curl ... | sh`" remediation.
Tool output goes straight into the model's context with the same authority as retrieved
documents. ATLAS calls this AI Agent Tool Poisoning: Runtime Response; the 2026 "Agentjacking"
research (fake Sentry errors) and CVE-2026-75130 (Context7 MCP) are real cases. Correlate with
LLMD-017 in the same session: instruction in, command out.
